topic: The Secret of Speed: Understanding Instantaneous Rate of Change & The Derivative
target_audience: High school seniors or first-year university students (Introductory Calculus)

sections.title: The Mystery of the Speed Trap
lecture_lines: Dash the cheetah sprints 100 meters in 4 seconds.
His average speed is exactly 25 meters per second.
We freeze-frame his journey at exactly 2.5 seconds.
Look closely at the position of his paws now.
How fast is he moving at this specific instant?
animations: A yellow (#FFFF00) circle representing Dash the cheetah moves horizontally across the screen.
The label 'Average Speed = 25 m/s' appears in white (#FFFFFF) below the path.
The motion freezes; a vertical cyan (#00FFFF) line marks the 2.5s position.
A white (#FFFFFF) circle outlines Dash's paws to focus the viewer's attention.
A flashing magenta (#FF00FF) question mark appears above the frozen cheetah.

sections.title: Prerequisite Check: The Slope of a Line
lecture_lines: Rate of change is the steepness of a line.
We calculate slope using rise divided by run.
For a hiker's steady path, this slope never changes.
animations: A white (#FFFFFF) straight line with a constant positive slope appears.
Two green (#00FF00) dots appear on the line at different intervals.
A yellow (#FFFF00) right triangle connects the dots, labeled 'Rise' and 'Run'.

sections.title: The Curved Path Problem
lecture_lines: Curves represent things that change speed over time.
At any point, the steepness is constantly shifting.
Our standard slope formula needs two points, not one.
animations: A white (#FFFFFF) curve representing a parabola y = 0.2x^2 appears.
A cyan (#00FFFF) small rectangle moves along the curve to simulate a car.
A yellow (#FFFF00) line segment follows the car, showing changing steepness.

sections.title: The Secant Line Bridge
lecture_lines: A secant line connects two points on a curve.
Its slope approximates the speed between these two moments.
But this average is still just a blurry guess.
animations: A white (#FFFFFF) curve y = x^2 appears with point P labeled at (1,1).
A green (#00FF00) point Q appears further along the curve at (2,4).
A yellow (#FFFF00) line connects P and Q, labeled 'Slope = 3'.

sections.title: The Limit: Zooming into Infinity
lecture_lines: Let's slide point Q closer to our target P.
The gap between them, called h, shrinks toward zero.
As Q approaches P, the secant line starts tilting.
It transforms into a tangent line touching one point.
This limit reveals the exact speed at point P.
animations: Point Q (#00FF00) slides down the curve toward point P (#FFFFFF).
The yellow (#FFFF00) secant line rotates to track the moving point Q.
A cyan (#00FFFF) horizontal bracket shows the distance 'h' shrinking to zero.
A white (#FFFFFF) text label shows the slope value decreasing towards 2.
Q merges with P, and the line becomes a green (#00FF00) Tangent Line.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
lecture_lines: We formalize this "zooming in" process with math.
The limit definition calculates slope as h vanishes.
This result is the derivative, denoted as f prime.
It provides a formula for slope at any moment.
Now we can calculate the cheetah's exact speedometer reading.
animations: The white (#FFFFFF) formula f'(x) = lim (h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h appears.
The 'f(x+h) - f(x)' part of the formula glows yellow (#FFFF00).
The 'h' in the denominator glows cyan (#00FFFF).
Green (#00FF00) text 'Instantaneous Rate' appears above the equal sign.
The formula transitions into f'(x) = 2x in white (#FFFFFF) text.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Beyond Speed
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure change in more than just physical movement.
They accurately predict power draw in your smartphone battery.
Calculus is the language of our constantly changing world.
animations: A white (#FFFFFF) battery icon outline appears on the screen.
A green (#00FF00) fill inside the battery slowly moves to the left.
A yellow (#FFFF00) arrow points to the decreasing edge, labeled 'Power Draw'.
